name: computer_screenshot
description: Capture the current screen and return it as an image, together with the list of visible windows. Coordinates in every computer_* tool refer to pixels of the most recent screenshot, which is 1280x1024 unless a region is given. Take a new screenshot after any action that changes the screen before you rely on positions again; layouts move when dialogs open, menus expand or windows are resized. Do not take screenshots in a tight loop: wait for the UI to settle with computer_wait when an operation is in progress.

region.description: Optional sub-rectangle to capture. Omit to capture the whole display.

display.description: Display index for multi-monitor setups. The primary display is 0.

name: computer_click
description: Move the pointer to a position and click. Use the coordinates of the element's center as seen in the latest screenshot. Prefer ui_click_element when you already have an element id from ui_find_element, because element ids survive small layout changes while raw coordinates do not. Double-clicks and triple-clicks are expressed with the clicks parameter. Hold modifier keys with modifiers, for example cmd-click to select several files in a file manager.

x.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate of the click target.

y.description: Vertical pixel coordinate of the click target.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the click.

name: computer_drag
description: Press the mouse button at a start point, move to an end point and release. Use it to move windows by their title bar, resize panes with splitters, select text ranges, or drag files between folders. Long drags across the screen should use a duration of at least 300 ms so that the target application registers intermediate pointer events.

x.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate, 0 at the left edge.

y.description: Vertical pixel coordinate, 0 at the top edge.

x.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate, 0 at the left edge.

y.description: Vertical pixel coordinate, 0 at the top edge.

button.description: Mouse button held during the drag.

duration_ms.description: How long the movement takes, in milliseconds.

name: computer_type_text
description: Type text into the element that currently has keyboard focus. Click or focus the target field first and verify the focus in a screenshot when it matters. The text is typed literally, including Unicode characters; it is not interpreted as key names, so use computer_key_press for shortcuts such as cmd+s. Set press_enter to submit a single-line field after typing.

delay_ms.description: Delay between keystrokes in milliseconds, for applications that drop fast input.

press_enter.description: Press Enter after the text has been typed.

name: computer_key_press
description: Press a key or a key combination. All keys in the list are pressed together in order and released in reverse order, so ["cmd", "shift", "t"] performs Command+Shift+T. Key names are lowercase: cmd, ctrl, alt, shift, enter, tab, esc, backspace, delete, space, up, down, left, right, home, end, pageup, pagedown, f1 to f12, or a single character. Use repeat to press the same combination several times.

repeat.description: How many times to press the combination.

name: computer_scroll
description: Scroll the content under a screen position. The amount is measured in wheel notches; one notch moves about three lines of text in most applications. Scroll inside the pane you want to move, not over a toolbar, because many applications route wheel events to the element under the pointer.

x.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate of the scroll position.

y.description: Vertical pixel coordinate of the scroll position.

name: computer_wait
description: Pause before the next action. Use it after starting a build, opening a large file or loading a page, instead of taking repeated screenshots. With until=idle the wait ends early when the screen stops changing; with until=window_change it ends when a window opens or closes.

seconds.description: Maximum time to wait, in seconds.

name: window_list
description: List open windows with their ids, titles, owning application, position, size and whether they are focused or minimized. Window ids are stable for the lifetime of a window and are used by window_focus, window_resize, window_arrange and ui_find_element.

app_name.description: Only list windows of this application, for example "Terminal".

include_minimized.description: Include minimized windows in the result.

name: window_focus
description: Bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus. If the window is minimized it is restored first. Focusing a window does not move it to another display.

window_id.description: Id of the window, as returned by window_list.

name: window_resize
description: Resize a window and optionally move it. Sizes are in pixels and are clamped to the visible area of the display. Some dialogs have a fixed size and ignore this call; the result reports the size that was actually applied.

window_id.description: Id of the window, as returned by window_list.

position.description: Optional new position of the window's top-left corner.

x.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate, 0 at the left edge.

y.description: Vertical pixel coordinate, 0 at the top edge.

name: window_arrange
description: Snap a window to a predefined layout: the left or right half, the top or bottom half, maximized, or centered at its current size. restore returns the window to the size it had before the last arrange call. Without window_id the focused window is arranged.

window_id.description: Id of the window to arrange. Defaults to the focused window.

name: app_launch
description: Start an application, or focus it if it is already running. Available applications include Code Editor, Terminal, Browser, Files, Settings, Notes, Calendar and Image Viewer. Arguments are passed to the application the same way as on a command line, for example a folder to open in Code Editor.

app_name.description: Name of the application to start.

wait_for_window.description: Return only after the first window of the application is visible.

name: clipboard_write
description: Replace the clipboard contents with plain text. Prefer typing short strings directly; use the clipboard for long or multi-line text that would be slow to type, then paste it with cmd+v.

text.description: Text to place on the clipboard.

name: ui_find_element
description: Search the accessibility tree of the visible windows for elements whose label, value or help text matches a query. Returns element ids, roles, labels and bounding boxes, best matches first. This is more reliable than reading positions from a screenshot for small controls such as checkboxes and tabs.

query.description: Text to look for in labels, values and help text. Matching is case-insensitive.

role.description: Restrict the search to one element role.

max_results.description: Maximum number of elements to return.

name: ui_click_element
description: Activate an element found with ui_find_element. press is a normal click, double_press opens items in lists, right_press opens the context menu, and focus moves keyboard focus without clicking.

name: image_zoom
description: Return an enlarged crop of the latest screenshot. Use it to read small text, inspect icons or check whether a checkbox is ticked before acting on it. The crop does not change the coordinate system used by other tools.

region.description: Area of the latest screenshot to enlarge.

name: fs_read_file
description: Read a text file from the workspace. Paths may be absolute or relative to /workspace/demo-app. Large files are returned in pages: use offset and limit (in lines) to read a specific part. Always read a file before editing it, and never guess its contents. Binary files are returned as base64 when encoding is base64.

path.description: Path of the file to read.

offset.description: First line to return, starting at 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return.

name: fs_write_file
description: Create or replace a file with the given content. Parent directories are created only when create_dirs is true. An existing file is replaced only when overwrite is true; otherwise the call fails, which protects against accidental data loss. Use fs_edit_file for small changes to existing files.

path.description: Path of the file to write.

content.description: Complete new content of the file.

overwrite.description: Replace the file if it already exists.

name: fs_edit_file
description: Apply exact text replacements to an existing file. Each edit replaces old_text with new_text; old_text must appear exactly once in the file unless replace_all is true, otherwise the whole call fails and the file is left unchanged. Edits are applied in order, so later edits see the result of earlier ones. Include enough surrounding context in old_text to make it unique.

path.description: Path of the file to edit.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of exactly one.

name: fs_list_dir
description: List the entries of a directory with their type, size and modification time. Use recursive with a small max_depth to get an overview of a project; the output is truncated after 2000 entries. Hidden files are skipped unless include_hidden is true.

include_hidden.description: Include entries whose names start with a dot.

max_depth.description: Maximum recursion depth when recursive is true.

name: fs_search_files
description: Find files by name with a glob pattern such as "**/*.yaml" or "src/**/test_*.py". This matches file names and paths only; it does not look inside files (use fs_grep for that). Results are sorted by modification time, newest first.

root.description: Directory to search from. Defaults to the workspace root.

max_results.description: Maximum number of paths to return.

include_hidden.description: Also match files inside hidden directories.

name: fs_grep
description: Search file contents with a regular expression and return matching lines with file names and line numbers. Narrow the search with path and glob; for example glob "*.py" searches Python files only. Use fs_search_files instead when you are looking for files by name.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to the workspace root.

glob.description: Only search files whose names match this glob.

context_lines.description: Lines of context to show before and after each match.

name: fs_move
description: Move or rename a file or directory. The destination's parent directory must exist. An existing destination is replaced only when overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it exists.

name: fs_delete
description: Delete one or more files or directories. Directories are deleted only when recursive is true. Deleted files cannot be recovered, so double-check the paths, and never delete anything outside the workspace.

recursive.description: Delete directories together with their contents.

name: shell_run
description: Run a shell command in a non-interactive bash session and return its exit code, stdout and stderr. The working directory defaults to /workspace/demo-app. Commands that wait for input will time out, so pass flags such as --yes where needed. Prefer the dedicated fs_* tools for reading, searching and editing files, and git_* tools for version control. Give a short description of what the command does.

timeout_s.description: Kill the command after this many seconds.

description.description: One sentence describing what the command does and why.

name: process_kill
description: Send a signal to a process started in this session, for example a development server that no longer responds. TERM asks the process to exit; use KILL only if TERM had no effect after a few seconds.

name: git_status
description: Show the current branch, the upstream tracking state and the staged, modified and untracked files of a repository. Run it before committing to make sure only the intended files are included.

repo_path.description: Repository root. Defaults to the workspace root.

name: git_diff
description: Show changes as a unified diff: unstaged changes by default, or staged changes when staged is true. Restrict the output to some files with files.

repo_path.description: Repository root. Defaults to the workspace root.

staged.description: Show staged changes instead of unstaged ones.

context_lines.description: Lines of context around each change.

name: git_commit
description: Create a commit. When files is given, exactly those paths are staged before committing; otherwise the current index is committed as it is. The message is used verbatim, including line breaks: the first line is the summary, followed by a blank line and the body.

amend.description: Amend the previous commit instead of creating a new one.

name: run_tests
description: Run the project's test suite or a subset of it and return a structured summary with failures, durations and the relevant part of the output. Use filter to run a single test file or test name while iterating, and the full suite before you report that a change is done.

filter.description: Runner-specific selection expression, for example a test name pattern.

timeout_s.description: Abort the run after this many seconds.

name: python_exec
description: Execute a short Python 3 snippet in a fresh interpreter and return stdout, stderr and the value of the last expression. Use it for quick calculations, data inspection or format conversions, not for long-running work. The interpreter has no network access.

name: browser_navigate
description: Open a URL in the browser, in the current tab or a new one, and wait until the page has loaded. Returns the final URL after redirects, the page title and the tab id. Use http_request instead when you only need the raw response of an API endpoint.

new_tab.description: Open the URL in a new tab.

name: browser_get_text
description: Return the visible text of the current page, or of the elements matching a CSS selector, with links listed at the end. Long pages are truncated to max_chars characters.

selector.description: CSS selector. Omit to read the whole page.

max_chars.description: Truncate the text after this many characters.

tab_id.description: Tab to read. Defaults to the active tab.

name: browser_click
description: Click an element on the page, identified by a CSS selector or by its visible text. Waits for the element to become visible and enabled before clicking, up to five seconds.

text.description: Visible text of the element, used when no selector is given.

tab_id.description: Tab to act in. Defaults to the active tab.

name: browser_fill_form
description: Fill several form fields at once and optionally submit the form. Each field is located by a CSS selector; text inputs are cleared before the value is entered, checkboxes accept "true" or "false", and select elements accept the visible option text.

submit.description: Submit the form after filling it.

tab_id.description: Tab to act in. Defaults to the active tab.

name: browser_close_tabs
description: Close browser tabs by id. Tab ids are shown in the tab strip and returned by browser_navigate. Closing the last tab leaves an empty browser window open.

tab_ids.description: Ids of the tabs to close.

name: http_request
description: Send an HTTP request and return the status code, headers and body. JSON bodies are serialized from json_body and the Content-Type header is set automatically. Only hosts on the local network and the documentation mirror are reachable. Use this instead of the browser for APIs, health checks and machine-readable endpoints.

query.description: Query parameters appended to the URL.

json_body.description: JSON request body for POST, PUT and PATCH.

name: web_search
description: Search the offline documentation mirror and return titles, URLs and short snippets. Use specific queries with library names and version numbers; open promising results with browser_navigate.

site.description: Restrict results to one documentation site, for example "docs.python.org".

recency.description: Only return pages updated within this period.

name: notes_create
description: Create a note in the Notes app. The body supports Markdown. Tags help to find the note later; pinned notes are shown at the top of the list.

body.description: Content of the note, in Markdown.

pinned.description: Pin the note to the top of the list.

name: calendar_create_event
description: Create an event in the local Calendar app. Times are ISO 8601 date-times in the workstation's time zone, for example 2026-11-03T10:00. A recurring event repeats with the given frequency and interval until count occurrences have been created.

reminders_min.description: Reminders, in minutes before the start.

recurrence.description: Repeat rule. Omit for a single event.

name: task_create
description: Add a task to the project task list. Use it to track follow-up work that is out of scope for the current change, so it is not forgotten.

due_date.description: Due date, ISO 8601 date such as 2026-11-15.

name: settings_set
description: Change a setting of an application, such as the editor's tab size or the terminal's font. Workspace settings apply to the current project only; user settings apply everywhere.

name: system_set_volume
description: Set the output volume of the workstation. level is a fraction between 0 (silent) and 1 (maximum); muting keeps the level so that unmuting restores it.

name: archive_create
description: Pack files and directories into an archive. The destination's extension should match the format. Higher compression levels are slower and rarely worth it for already-compressed data such as images.

destination.description: Path of the archive to create.
